route.gap_parts: Budget: Think-SFT + cue hits the cap on 89 of 328 hard problems, and its cut answers are unfinished work it would close (at cap 32,768, 91 of 93 finish and 23 are right, result-c8b994). If the boundary ends answers before 16,384, up to about 23 answers on hard328 come back (I forecast 10 to 15) and about 5 on MATH-500 (24 of its 46 MATH-500 errors are cap hits, result-bf6124). Answer statement: a single short final answer after </think> takes away the lines after 'Answer:' that grader v3 rejects (16 of 74 finished-wrong answers end on a line equal to the gold, result-818c20). That is up to about 4 per 500 on MATH-500 and about 0 on hard328. Loop: 0, since T 1.0 has no loops. Reliability and capability: unchanged, because precision on finished answers stays the same.
route.why: Think-SFT was trained to end its reasoning at </think> and then write one short answer and end-of-text. With the base's raw cue there is no such boundary, so after solving it keeps re-checking until the cap and the answer scores zero. Putting the boundary back makes it stop where it was trained to stop, with the same precision on finished answers.
